top3.title: Don't Torture a Duckling
top3.venue: PFS Film Society Center, 1412 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102
top3.why: Lucio Fulci's 1972 giallo "Don't Torture a Duckling" — a brutal, hallucinatory murder mystery set in a superstition-soaked southern Italian village — gets a rare theatrical outing at the Film Society's Chestnut Street screen. top3.title: Dread Beat an Blood
top3.venue: Bok Auditorium, 800 Mifflin St, Philadelphia, PA 19148, USA
top3.why: Lightbox Film Center screens a new restoration of Dread Beat an Blood (1978), Franco Rosso's documentary portrait of dub poet Linton Kwesi Johnson and Black British political life in Thatcher-era London — a landmark of Black British cinema that's been nearly impossible to see for decades. At Bok Auditorium in South Philly.

top3.title: Healing the Wounds of Racism & Building Beloved Communities
top3.venue: Philadelphia Ethical Society, 1906 Rittenhouse Square, Philadelphia, PA 19103
top3.why: Playback for Change, a multiracial improvisational theater company, brings its Playback Theatre practice to the Ethical Society's Sunday Platform: audience members tell a story from their own life, choose actors to play the roles, and watch it recreated live on stage. Free and open to the public — a genuinely participatory way to sit with the subject rather than a lecture about it.

top3.venue: Studio 34 (4522 Baltimore Ave. Philadelphia, PA 19143)

Genuinely strange, genuinely heavy, and not reducible to one metal subgenre. West Philly, on the Route 34 trolley along Baltimore Ave.
